parts.label: (a)
parts.text:
Sodium chlorate(I), $\text{NaClO}$, is the active ingredient in commercial bleach. The concentration of chlorate(I) ions was determined by titration.

- $10.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ of a bleach solution was diluted to $250\text{ cm}^{3}$ in a volumetric flask using distilled water.
- Dilute sulfuric acid and an excess of potassium iodide solution were added to a $25.0\text{ cm}^{3}$ portion of this solution to liberate iodine.
- The resulting solution required $20.80\text{ cm}^{3}$ of $0.100\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$ aqueous sodium thiosulfate solution to react with the iodine produced.

The titration reactions are shown.

$$\text{ClO}^{-} + 2\text{I}^{-} + 2\text{H}^{+} \rightarrow \text{I}_{2} + \text{Cl}^{-} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$

$$\text{I}_{2} + 2\text{S}_{2}\text{O}_{3}^{2-} \rightarrow 2\text{I}^{-} + \text{S}_{4}\text{O}_{6}^{2-}$$

Calculate the concentration, in $\text{mol dm}^{-3}$, of $\text{ClO}^{-}$ ions in the bleach solution.

parts.label: (b)(i)
parts.stem: An indicator was used in the thiosulfate-iodine titration.
parts.text: Name a suitable indicator for this titration.

parts.label: (b)(ii)
parts.text: State the expected colour change you would observe at the end-point in this titration.

parts.label: (b)(iii)
parts.text: State when in the procedure you would add the indicator.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text:
The concentration of chlorate(I) ions can also be determined by adding an excess of hydrogen peroxide to the sample of bleach and measuring the volume of oxygen gas produced.

$$\text{H}_{2}\text{O}_{2} + \text{NaClO} \rightarrow \text{NaCl} + \text{O}_{2} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O}$$

{{figure:visual_auto_01.png}}

Calculate the concentration of $\text{ClO}^{-}$ ions in this bleach solution.

parts.label: (d)(i)
parts.stem:
Trichlorocyanuric acid, $\text{C}_{3}\text{Cl}_{3}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{3}$, acts as a chlorine buffer and disinfectant for swimming pools. It reacts with water to give chloric(I) acid, $\text{HClO}$.

$$\text{C}_{3}\text{Cl}_{3}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{3} + 3\text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{C}_{3}\text{H}_{3}\text{N}_{3}\text{O}_{3} + 3\text{HClO}$$
parts.text: Write the expression for $K_{\text{c}}$ for this equilibrium.

parts.label: (d)(ii)
parts.text:
In outdoor swimming pools, the $\text{HClO}$ is decomposed by sunlight. The decomposition of $\text{HClO}$ is a redox reaction which forms a gas that relights a glowing splint.

Describe and explain the effect of the decomposition of $\text{HClO}$ on the equilibrium in (d). State the effect on $K_{\text{c}}$.

parts.label: (d)(iii)
parts.text:
The decomposition of $\text{HClO}$ is a redox reaction.

Suggest an equation for this reaction.

parts.label: (e)(i)
parts.stem:
The buffer solution in blood is a mixture of carbonic acid, $\text{H}_{2}\text{CO}_{3}$, and hydrogencarbonate ions, $\text{HCO}_{3}^{-}$. Healthy blood has a pH of 7.40.

$$\text{H}_{2}\text{CO}_{3} + \text{H}_{2}\text{O} \rightleftharpoons \text{HCO}_{3}^{-} + \text{H}_{3}\text{O}^{+} \quad K_{\text{a}} = 7.94 \times 10^{-7}\text{ mol dm}^{-3}$$
parts.text: Explain how this buffer system acts to control the blood pH. Include equations in your answer.

parts.label: (e)(ii)
parts.text:
A patient's blood has a $[\text{HCO}_{3}^{-}]:[\text{H}_{2}\text{CO}_{3}]$ ratio of 9.5:1.

Calculate the pH of the patient's blood.
